# The Neuroprotective Activities of the Novel Multi-Target Iron-Chelators in Models of Alzheimer’s Disease, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis and Aging

**Авторы:** Kupershmidt Lana, Youdim Moussa B. H.

**Журнал:** Cells (2023)

**DOI:** 10.3390/cells12050763


## Abstract

The concept of chelation therapy as a valuable therapeutic approach in neurological disorders led us to develop multi-target, non-toxic, lipophilic, brain-permeable compounds with iron chelation and anti-apoptotic properties for neurodegenerative diseases, such as Parkinson’s disease (PD), Alzheimer’s disease (AD), age-related dementia and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
source_units.reason: article_metadata_header

source_units.text: Herein, we reviewed our two most effective such compounds, M30 and HLA20, based on a multimodal drug design paradigm.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The compounds have been tested for their mechanisms of action using animal and cellular models such as APP/PS1 AD transgenic (Tg) mice, G93A-SOD1 mutant ALS Tg mice, C57BL/6 mice, Neuroblastoma × Spinal Cord-34 (NSC-34) hybrid cells, a battery of behavior tests, and various immunohistochemical and biochemical techniques.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: These novel iron chelators exhibit neuroprotective activities by attenuating relevant neurodegenerative pathology, promoting positive behavior changes, and up-regulating neuroprotective signaling pathways.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Taken together, these results suggest that our multifunctional iron-chelating compounds can upregulate several neuroprotective-adaptive mechanisms and pro-survival signaling pathways in the brain and might function as ideal drugs for neurodegenerative disorders, such as PD, AD, ALS, and aging-related cognitive decline, in which oxidative stress and iron-mediated toxicity and dysregulation of iron homeostasis have been implicated.

source_units.text:
Brain-Iron Homeostasis, Oxidative Stress and Neurodegeneration

The etiology of neurodegenerative diseases is not yet well understood, although cerebrovascular atrophy that leads to brain ischemia may be a potential pathogenic factor for age-related dementia [1].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, accumulating evidence has shown that iron-dependent oxidative stress (OS), increased iron levels, and monoamine oxidase (MAO)-B activity, as well as reduced antioxidant levels and activities in the brain, may be major pathogenic factors in neurodegenerative diseases [2].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: It is well established that iron is an essential cofactor for many key proteins involved in the normal function of neuronal tissues and is normally involved in oxygen transport, storage and activation, electron transport, and many important metabolic processes [3].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In the central nervous system (CNS), iron is essential for multiple functions, including gene expression, DNA synthesis, neurotransmission, myelination, and mitochondrial electron transport (Figure 1) [4].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Iron incorporation and transport in the brain are regulated by the interaction between the endothelial cells and astrocytes: the transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) in the luminal membrane of endothelial cells binds Fe3+-loaded transferrin and internalizes this complex in endosomes, where Fe3+ is reduced to Fe2+.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The latter is transported to the cytosol by the divalent metal transporter-1 (DMT1) and exported into the extracellular fluid by the iron exporter, ferroportin [5].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Alternatively, it has been proposed that the transferrin-TfR1 complex may be transported from the luminal to the abluminal surface by an iron release [6].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Ceruloplasmin, expressed in the astrocyte, oxidizes newly released Fe2+ to Fe3+, which binds to transferrin in the brain interstitial fluid [5,6,7].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Fe2+ can also bind to adenosine triphosphate (ATP) or citrate and be transported as non-transferrin-bound iron (NTBI), which is the source of iron for astrocytes and oligodendrocytes, which do not express TfR1 [5,6].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Yet, there is increasing evidence that iron accumulation and deposition can cause a vast range of neurodegenerative disorders of the CNS [8,9,10].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Free iron can induce OS because of its interaction with H2O2 in the Fenton reaction, thus resulting in an increased formation of hydroxyl free radicals.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Free radical-related OS causes molecular damage that can then lead to a critical failure of biological functions, protein modification, misfolding and aggregation and ultimately cell death [3,11,12,13].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Indeed, in aging and various neurodegenerative diseases, such as Parkinson’s disease (PD), Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Huntington’s disease (HD), amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and multiple sclerosis (MS), iron was shown to accumulate at the site of the lesion, thus suggesting having a role in neuronal death processes [8,10,14,15,16,17].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Iron also has been shown to accumulate in the aged brain mainly in the form of ferritin, in the microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and the various regions, including the globus pallidus, substantia nigra, putamen, caudate nucleus, dentate nucleus and frontal cortex [4].

source_units.text:
Alzheimer’s Disease

AD is the most prevalent neurodegenerative disease in the elderly population, and it has been estimated that about 5% of adults over 65 years are affected by this devastating disease [18].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Its predominant clinical manifestation is progressive memory deterioration and other changes in brain function, including disordered behavior and impairment in language, comprehension, and visual-spatial skills [19].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The neuropathology of AD is characterized by several features, including extracellular deposition of amyloid β (Aβ) peptide-containing plaques in the cerebral cortical regions, accompanied by the presence of intracellular neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) and a progressive loss of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons leading to reductions in cholinergic markers, such as acetylcholine levels, choline acetyltransferase (ChAT) and muscarinic and nicotinic acetylcholine receptor binding [20,21].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Additionally, there is accumulating evidence demonstrating that many cytotoxic signals in the AD brain can initiate apoptotic processes, including OS, inflammation, and iron accumulation [22,23,24].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Iron is significantly concentrated around amyloid senile plaques and NFTs, leading to alterations in the pattern of the interaction between iron regulatory proteins 1 and 2 (IRP1 and IRP2) and their iron-responsive element (IRE) and disruption in the sequestration and storage of iron [25,26].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Additionally, high levels of iron have been reported in the amyloid plaques of the Tg2576 mouse model for AD, resembling those seen in the brains of AD patients [27].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition to iron accumulation in senile plaques, it was demonstrated that the amount of iron present in the AD neuropil is twice that found in the neuropil of non-demented brains [25].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Further studies have suggested that iron accumulation could be an important contributor to the OS damage of AD pathology, and thus, the neurons in AD brains experience high oxidative load [28,29,30,31].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Indeed, it was found that NFTs and senile plaques contain redox-active transition metals and may exert pro-oxidant/antioxidant activities, depending on the balance among neuronal antioxidants and reductants [32].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Post-mortem analyses of AD patients’ brains have revealed activation of two enzymatic indicators of cellular OS: heme oxygenase (HO-1) [33] and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidase [34].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, HO-1 was greatly enhanced in neurons and astrocytes of the hippocampus and cerebral cortex of Alzheimer’s subjects, co-localizing to senile plaques and NFTs.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: It was reported that ribosomal RNA provided a binding site for redox-active iron and served as a redox center within the cytoplasm of vulnerable neurons in the AD brain prior to the appearance of morphological changes indicating neurodegeneration [29].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Many studies suggested that iron homeostasis is disrupted in AD [25,35,36].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, abnormal localization of the IRP1, and IRP2, which was shown in AD, might be linked to impaired iron homeostasis in AD [37].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, this is likely to be a secondary effect via another process, such as increased HO-1 activity in response to cellular OS [38] or a decrease in heme bioavailability resulting from Aβ binding to heme, increasing free iron levels [39].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The location of the iron-transport protein, transferrin, in senile plaques, instead of its regular location in the cytosol of oligodendrocytes, may indicate that transferring becomes trapped within plaques while transporting iron between cells [35].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Indeed, Loeffler and collaborators [40] reported on diminished transferrin/iron ratios in various brain regions of AD patients compared with normal elderly controls, indicating dysregulation of iron homeostasis.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, higher transferrin C2 allele occurrence has been described in AD compared with normal controls [41].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Previous studies assessing the effect of certain genes coding for proteins involved in iron metabolism, such as hemochromatosis (HFE) [42] and transferring C2 gene variants, showed a high fold risk of developing AD in aged bicarriers [43].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, the mediator of iron uptake by cells, melanotransferrin and the iron-storage protein ferritin, are altered in AD and are expressed within reactive microglial cells that are present both in and around senile plaques [42].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: At the biochemical level, iron was demonstrated to facilitate the aggregation of Aβ and induce aggregation of the major constituent of neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs), hyperphosphorylated tau protein [28,44].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: It was suggested that the toxicity of Aβ is mediated, at least in part, via redox-active iron; neuronal toxicity was significantly attenuated when Aβ was pretreated with the natural prototype iron chelator/radical scavenger, desferrioxamine (DFO), while conversely, toxicity was restored to original levels following incubation of Aβ with excess free iron [45].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, previous in vitro studies demonstrated that Aβ has a high affinity for iron, and the iron-binding sites are in the hydrophilic N-terminal part of the peptide [46].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Furthermore, the presence of redox-available iron in association with pathological lesions and increased OS strongly support the notion that oxidative damage plays an important role in the pathogenesis of AD [31].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Iron regulates amyloid precursor protein (APP) translation via functional IRE.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Another molecular link between iron metabolism and AD pathogenesis was provided by Rogers et al. [47], who described the presence of an IRE-type II in the 5′ untranslated region (5′UTR) of the APP transcript encoding the Alzheimer’s APP (51 to 94 from the 5′-cap site).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The APP mRNA IRE is located immediately upstream of the interleukin-1 responsive acute box domain (101 to 146) [23].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, APP 5′UTR is selectively responsive to intracellular iron levels in a pattern that reflects iron-dependent regulation of intracellular APP synthesis.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This signifies the APP molecule as metalloproteinase, which resembles that of the iron-associated protein ferritin, a central iron-storage molecule, and the iron-regulated transporter protein-1 (IREG-1), which transports iron from enterocytes into the bloodstream [48,49,50].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Indeed, iron levels were shown to regulate mRNA translation of APP holo-protein in astrocytes [47,51] and neuroblastoma cells by a pathway like iron control in the translation of the ferritin-L and -H mRNAs by IREs in their 5′UTRs [50].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: An additional study demonstrated that IRP1, but not IRP2, selectively bound the APP IRE in human neural cells [52].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Recently, Duce and coworkers [53] have identified APP as a functional ferroxidase like ceruloplasmin.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Ferroxidases prevent OS caused by Fenton and Haber–Weiss reactions by oxidizing Fe2+ to Fe3+.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Both holo-APP and soluble forms of APP (sAPP) species were found to have interactions with ferroportin to regulate iron transport from neurons [53].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The authors suggested that APP, by discharging neurons of Fe2+, may play an important role in preventing iron-mediated OS through two alternative domains: a heme-oxygenase-inhibitory domain that prevents the release of Fe2+ from heme and the ferroxidase domain, which oxidizes Fe2+ to Fe3+ [53].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, iron has been shown to facilitate Aβ and hyperphosphorylated tau aggregation.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: At the biochemical level, Aβ is defined as a redox-active metalloprotein that is precipitated by interactions with neocortical metal ions, especially zinc, copper, and iron resulting in its auto-aggregation and oligomerization [54,55].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Three histidine and one tyrosine residues at the hydrophilic N terminus of the peptide are crucial for metal ion binding to the peptide [54,55].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Regarding the interaction with iron, it was found that Fe3+ influences the formation of amyloid fibrils of Aβ1–42 [56] and Aβ25–35 [57].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The interaction of redox-active Fe3+ with Aβ fibrils results in their chemical reduction and concomitant generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), causing lipid membrane peroxidation, DNA breakdown, and protein oxidation [44,58,59,60].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Partial aggregated and oligomerized intracellular Aβ was documented to be cytotoxic and synaptotoxic in cell culture and in vivo [45,61,62,63,64].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In vitro, iron was demonstrated to enhance Aβ toxicity since the removal of iron from the culture medium or the inclusion of adequate iron chelators reduced or blocked Aβ-induced toxicity while overloading cells with iron-potentiated neuronal toxicity [45,65].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, Fe3+ in culture media may bind to soluble Aβ and, given its amphiphilic nature, may subsequently attach to the cell membrane, thereby inducing oxidative injury [66,67].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Iron may enhance Aβ toxicity by preventing the formation of mature well-ordered fibrillar aggregation of Aβ [68].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Consequently, it has been suggested that abnormal iron deposition, such as in AD plaques, can interact with Aβ to mediate free radical-induced neurotoxicity and may account, in part, for the widespread oxidative damage in AD brains, accelerating the pathological process [31].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, iron was found to accumulate in NFTs [31,69].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Fe3+ can bind hyperphosphorylated tau and induce its aggregation in vitro, leading to the formation of NFTs in AD.

source_units.text:
Iron-Chelating Therapeutic Strategy in AD

Currently, numerous clinical trials have demonstrated the safety and efficacy of acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (AChEIs) in the treatment of AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Yet, their benefits in AD as symptomatic drugs are likely to be more complex than a simple replacement of lost acetylcholine [70,71,72,73].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: As reviewed previously, there is growing preclinical evidence that AChEIs have minor therapeutic effects and may block some of the fundamental neurodegenerative processes involved in AD [74].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Thus, much of pharmacology efforts are allocated towards other therapeutic approaches for AD, such as targeting iron neurotoxicity.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Previous studies have demonstrated that metal-chelating compounds confer a potential to prevent metal-induced ROS, OS, and Aβ peptide aggregation [75].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Recently, several studies have reported a survey of various metal chelators, including restoring iron homeostasis compounds, that are potentially useful for the treatment of AD [76,77,78,79,80].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The iron chelator, DFO, has been reported in a single clinical study to slow down the progression of AD dementia [81], to prevent the formation of β-pleated sheets of Aβ1–42 and dissolve preformed β-pleated sheets of plaque-like amyloid in vitro [56].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Some clinical success has also been achieved with another metal-complexing agent, clioquinol [82].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Nonetheless, the long-term treatment of clioquinol (first generation, PBT1) caused side effects ending up with subacute myelopathic neuropathy and no significant effect on the cognition of AD patients [83,84,85].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: However, a Phase IIa clinical trial reported positive results with the safe use of the second generation of clioquinol, PBT2, which significantly reduced Aβ plaque deposits and improved the cognitive behavior of AD patients [86,87,88].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In preclinical experiments, oral administration of clioquinol was reported to inhibit Aβ accumulation in an AD transgenic mouse model via its actions as a metal chelator [89], and clioquinol was recently demonstrated to chelate metal ions from metal-Aβ species and cause conformational transformation of Aβ aggregates [90].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The identification of an IRE in the 5′UTR of the APP transcript led to a novel therapeutic approach aimed at reducing amyloidosis by several FDA-pre-approved drugs targeted to the IRE in the APP mRNA 5′UTR [91,92].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For example, DFO, tetrathiomolybdate (Cu2+ chelator), and dimercaptopropanol (Pb2+ and Hg2+ chelator) were found to suppress APP holoprotein expression and lower Aβ peptide secretion [91,92].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, the bi-functional molecule XH-1, which contains both amyloid-binding and metal-chelating moieties, was shown to reduce APP expression in SH-SY5Y cells and attenuate cerebral Aβ in APP and PS1 double-transgenic mice [93].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Additional drug classes were also reported to suppress the APP 5′UTR and limit APP expression, including antibiotics, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), and other selective receptor antagonists and agonists [92].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Up to date, available drug treatments are symptomatic with no disease-modifying effects on the underlying progressive processes in AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A new field of therapeutic strategy is poly-pharmacology and multiple-target molecules, suggesting that drugs acting at a single target may be insufficient for the treatment of AD, which is characterized by the coexistence of several pathologies [94,95,96,97,98,99].

source_units.text: Aging
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Aging of the brain has been demonstrated to be the main risk factor for AD.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The association between brain aging and AD is continuously discussed.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: One observation holds that AD results when brain aging goes beyond a threshold.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: According to recent criteria, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) Aβ changes are the primary link between AD and brain aging [100].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Evidence for the role of iron in aged-related pathologies has been demonstrated by studies showing that concentrations of non-heme iron increase in the putamen, motor cortex, prefrontal cortex, sensory cortex, and thalamus during the first 30–35 years of life [101].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Recent studies have also shown that levels of ferritin, the major iron storage protein, in older individuals were higher than in younger controls in the frontal cortex, caudate nucleus, putamen, substantia nigra, and globus pallidus [10,102].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A study comparing the cellular and regional distribution of ferritin and iron between young and aged rats has indicated that in the normal aging brain, there is an intracellular accumulation of iron in neurons [103].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A recent study involving human subjects demonstrated the correlation between iron content, as measured by quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and cognitive impairments in elderly participants.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Accordingly, the R2 MRI parameter affected by changes in brain iron concentration and water content was different in elderly participants with mild to severe levels of cognitive impairment compared with healthy controls [104], suggesting that iron misregulation might play a role in the decline in cognitive function observed in aged individuals.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Recently, DFO and other metal-chelating agents have also been investigated as possible therapeutic agents for age-related neuropathology.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: For example, the effect of DFO was evaluated on age-related recognition memory deficits in aged Wistar rats.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: DFO-treated rats showed normal recognition memory in a novel object recognition task, while the saline group showed long-term recognition memory deficits.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The results showed that DFO was able to reverse age-induced recognition memory deficits and reduced oxidative damage to proteins in the cortex and hippocampus, indicating that iron chelators might prevent age-related memory dysfunction.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: ALS, commonly referred to as Lou Gehrig’s disease, is a relentlessly progressive neurologic disorder with an estimated prevalence of four to six cases per 100,000 [105].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The onset of ALS is most common in midlife (usually between ages 45 and 60), with a typical disease course of 1 to 5 years.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Most ALS cases (90%) are of unknown etiology and are classified as sporadic.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The remaining 10% of cases are familial, and 20% of them are attributed to mutation in the superoxide dismutase-1 (SOD1) gene [106].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Both sporadic and familial forms of ALS are clinically and pathologically similar, suggesting possible common pathogenesis and the final pathway of neurodegeneration.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The molecular pathogenesis of ALS is poorly understood, contributing to the lack of effective system-based therapies to treat this disease.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Investigations have implied that ALS is a multifactorial and multisystemic disease that arises through a combination of several mechanisms that act by concurring damage inside motor neurons and their neighboring non-motor cells, including protein misfolding and aggregation; genetic factors; OS damage and mitochondrial dysfunction; defective axonal transport; excitotoxicity, and neuroinflammation [107,108].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In ALS patients, an imbalance in ROS production, either caused directly by mutant SOD1 or indirectly by other mechanisms, could be responsible for an altered iron homeostasis [109].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: How this is accomplished is not known.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: An intriguing hypothesis is based on the observation that superoxide radicals, if not detoxified appropriately, can inactivate enzymes containing Fe–S clusters by oxidizing one Fe and causing its release from the cluster [110].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The increased Fe demand of the SOD-defective cells may reflect its aim to continuously reconstitute the “missing” Fe in the Fe–S clusters.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: An early indication of the role of iron in the pathogenesis of ALS was provided by the elevated iron levels in the CNS of both sporadic and familial forms [111,112,113].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In addition, the expression of ferritin was induced at the last stages of the disease in the SOD1-G93A transgenic mouse (which develops symptoms and pathology like those of ALS patients), indicating high iron concentrations [107].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In line with this, it was reported that transferrin is localized in Bunina bodies of spinal cord neurons from ALS patients [114,115], suggesting the involvement of transferrin in the formation of these inclusions.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Interestingly, in transgenic mice expressing the wild-type SOD1 or SOD1-active mutant enzyme, G93A-SOD1, the expression of TfR and IRP1, a positive transcriptional regulator of TfR, were positively modulated in response to increased SOD1 mutation [114].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Jeong and collaborators [116] recently described the dysregulation of the iron homeostasis mechanism in the CNS in the G37R-SOD1 transgenic mice model of ALS, suggesting that iron chelation therapy might be useful for the treatment of ALS.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: A defect in the HFE gene, which was previously associated with iron-overload diseases, hemochromatosis, and AD, is currently associated with ALS [117].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The protein normally made by the HFE gene is thought to limit the uptake of iron by cells, protect against OS, and possibly dampen inflammatory reactions.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: An increased incidence of HFE mutation was reported in ALS patients [118].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The presence of this mutation was shown to disrupt the expression of tubulin and actin at the protein levels, potentially consistent with the disruption of axonal transport seen in ALS and associated with a decrease in SOD1 expression [118].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Therapeutic Strategies in ALS
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Treatment of ALS has been fueled in part by frustration over the shortcomings of the symptomatic drugs available because these are incapable of slowing the progression of the disease and neuronal degeneration.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Regrettably, the single drug approved for use in ALS, riluzole, a membrane-stabilizing drug, only slightly prolongs survival [119].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Currently, >150 different potential therapeutic agents or strategies have been tested in transgenic ALS mice, according to published trials [108].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: This list involves 108 pharmacotherapies, 14 gene or antisense therapies, nine cell transplantations, three immunizations, and seven dietary or lifestyle regimens.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Ferrous iron (Fe2+) is oxidized to ferric iron (Fe3+) through a reaction with hydrogen peroxide (H2O2).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The by-products of this reaction are the hydroxyl anion (OH−) and the hydroxyl radical (OH).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Consequently, the antioxidant GSH is significantly reduced, resulting in cell death.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Iron chelators and radical scavengers can inhibit the Fenton reaction and enhance antioxidant activity.
